transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-04-10 15:30 UTC
- Duration: 47 minutes
- Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Leah Armstrong (Redwood SE), Drew Matthews (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Singh (CTO - Novella), Carlos Rios (Head of Platform), Ellen Park (SRE), Jorge Alvarado (Data Scientist)

Summary:
- Novella is evaluating Redwood for a low-latency, high-throughput inference surface for clinical trial annotation and patient triage workflows. Primary concern: p95 latency at 300-600ms for streaming chat endpoints under mixed small/large token outputs, with spikes up to 600 concurrent streams.
- They want guidance on Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for data residency, cost, and predictable SLOs.
- Action items and a short pilot (2-4 week) were agreed as next steps.

Topics covered:
- Current infra & model: Novella runs open LLMs finetuned for medical NER, ~7B and 30B variants; mixed throughput: 20-60 tokens/sec for long generation, many short completions.
- Goals: p95 <= 600ms for short replies (<128 tokens) under 200-300 concurrent users; burst readiness to 600 concurrent for 5-10 minutes during morning batch ingestion.
- Telemetry wanted: per-token latency, batching benefits, KV-cache hit rates, streaming chunk latency, multi-region failover.
- Security questions: SOC2 Type II, customer-managed KMS, VPC/private control plane options.

Transcript body:
[00:00:03] Samir Patel: hey everyone thanks for carving out time. um quick intro from redwood side — i'm samir, ae — with leah and drew from solutions.
[00:00:12] Dr. Maya Singh: thanks, Maya here. i'll jump in, char, char, sorry — Maya from Novella. big picture we want to make sure inference doesn't become the bottleneck for our triage ui.
[00:00:25] Carlos Rios: yeah our main metric is p95 latency on the chat flow, most responses are short, often 40-80 tokens. sometimes longer, like 400 tokens for summaries.
[00:00:38] Leah Armstrong: got it. when you say p95 target what's your num — like 200ms, 1s?
[00:00:42] Dr. Maya Singh: we're aiming for 300-600ms p95 for short replies, and under 2s for the longer summary jobs. cost matters but it's second to reliability.
[00:00:52] Ellen Park: also security — must be SOC2, SSO, and we need a KMS integration for keys. private deployment is on the table if hosted can't meet our residency needs.
[00:01:05] Drew Matthews: noted. quick question on model footprint — you mentioned 7B and 30B variants. are you running both in prod or only 7B for interactive?
[00:01:14] Jorge Alvarado: we use 7B for most live chat; 30B is used for nightly batch summarization and some heavy context tasks. we can provide sample prompts and a token distribution.
[00:01:23] Samir Patel: perfect — that's the kind of profile Leah will use for the token/sec baselines.
[00:01:30] [00:01:30] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[00:01:34] Leah Armstrong: ok, technical constraints — are you comfortable with GPU pods, or do you have to be on-prem?
[00:01:40] Carlos Rios: we prefer cloud but need data residency in eu-west for the european cohort. hosting options: hosted api if it meets p95 and we get SOC2 and KMS; else dedicated eu-west zone or private vpc.
[00:01:55] Dr. Maya Singh: and we need predictable throughput for daily data loads — like a morning 30-minute burst where 400 requests come in surges, and then steady state of ~150rps? i mean rps for short requests.
[00:02:10] Leah Armstrong: okay that maps to burst capacity. Redwood Dedicated has reserved pools and burst options, and our routing can fall back to cheaper variants if the exact shape is exceeded.
[00:02:21] Samir Patel: to set expectations — for 7B streaming short replies on a typical A100-like pool p95 is often sub-500ms with continuous batching tuned. but it really depends on per-request sequence lengths and how much prefix caching, kv-cache hits you get.
[00:02:36] Ellen Park: what's kv-cache? we've heard of kv store but not this exact term.
[00:02:40] Drew Matthews: kv-cache is the key-value attention cache — it avoids re-encoding prior tokens for streaming chat and can drastically reduce token latency for long conversations, especially with many retries/edits.
[00:02:52] Jorge Alvarado: how often do you see bad transcriptions on the streaming boundary? our UI is very sensitive to chunk jitter.
[00:02:58] Leah Armstrong: there's jitter if your network is flaky, but our streaming plumbing minimizes chunk boundaries. we measure per-chunk RTT; typical chunk-to-client latency is ~50-120ms depending on region.
[00:03:10] [00:03:10] Speaker 2: hmm
[00:03:15] Carlos Rios: quick question about quantization — we've been told quantiza tion might change accuracy for our med NER. is that safe?
[00:03:22] Drew Matthews: we have quant profiles we recommend by workload; for NER often 4-bit quant can be okay for 7B but you should validate on your evals. Redwood Optimize gives recommendations and estimated cost savings.
[00:03:36] Dr. Maya Singh: ok. procurement question — what is the minimum committed for Dedicated?
[00:03:40] Samir Patel: typical reserved capacity starts at a monthly commitment for a modest GPU pool; i'll share the tiers. for pilots we can do a short evaluation with ephemeral reserved capacity to hit your p95 targets and then size.
[00:03:52] Ellen Park: and for Private on-prem, do you require a control-plane connection?
[00:03:56] Leah Armstrong: for Private we offer a customer-managed control plane option and an air-gapped option for regulated workloads. keys can live in your KMS/HSM.
[00:04:06] Jorge Alvarado: what telemetry would you need from us to run an accurate sizing?
[00:04:10] Leah Armstrong: sample prompts, token length distribution, concurrent user patterns (typical and burst), and a handful of example long-run jobs. plus an SRE contact for networking.
[00:04:22] Dr. Maya Singh: we'll put that together.
[00:04:25] [00:04:25] Samir Patel: on the benchmarking side — leah, do you want to outline the short baseline we agreed?
[00:04:29] Leah Armstrong: yeah. we'll run: (1) 15-min steady-state test at target concurrency (200-300) with mix of short/long; (2) 10-min burst to 600 concurrent with realistic token distribution; (3) a streaming-specific test measuring chunk latency and per-token throughput. we'll collect p50/p95/p99 and token/sec and KV cache hit rates.
[00:04:51] Carlos Rios: do you do these in our network or on redwood infra? we need this to reflect our latency to region.
[00:04:57] Leah Armstrong: best is to run with your region endpoints — we can run from a probe inside your VPC for private or dedicated, or we can run tests hitting the hosted eu-west endpoint to measure real-world.
[00:05:08] Ellen Park: we will need the test harness and a short runbook.
[00:05:12] Samir Patel: i'll share the harness repo link and a runbook, and leah will coordinate the runs.
[00:05:17] [00:05:17] Jorge Alvarado: can you share the benchmark spreadsheet template?
[00:05:20] Samir Patel: yes, sending a tco + benchmark template. link: https://drive.google.com/redwood/novella-bench-template (note: placeholder in notes)
[00:05:28] Dr. Maya Singh: on the architecture side — if we go dedicated, can we pin 7B to dedicated and have 30B on a different pool? we don't want the 30B to steal capacity.
[00:05:36] Drew Matthews: yes, we support model pinning and route policies so you can isolate workloads. also automatic fallback to smaller variants is configurable.
[00:05:46] Ellen Park: about cost, do you have ballpark numbers for 7B streaming and per-token cost?
[00:05:51] Samir Patel: ballpark: hosted per-token is competitive but with variability. Dedicated lowers per-token with reserved units; i'll include per-hour pool costs and estimated per-token numbers in the spreadsheet.
[00:05:59] [00:05:59] Speaker 3: (crosstalk)
[00:06:02] Carlos Rios: i've got a security question: audit logs and traceability — do you provide immutable logs for model requests?
[00:06:08] Leah Armstrong: yes we record audit logs, optionally long-retention; for Private we can integrate with your SIEM and ship logs to customer buckets.
[00:06:16] Dr. Maya Singh: wonderful. one more: do you have references in healthcare / med-tech?
[00:06:21] Samir Patel: we do, i can share anonymized case studies; i'll include one with p95 targets similar to yours.
[00:06:27] [00:06:27] Jorge Alvarado: ok what about warmup/cold starts for streaming sessions — how long to cold start a GPU worker for 7B?
[00:06:33] Drew Matthews: cold start depends on model load time and whether weights are cached. on Dedicated with kept-warm policy, cold starts can be sub-5s; with aggressive scale-to-zero, it may be tens of seconds. we recommend keep-warm for that morning burst use-case.
[00:06:48] Ellen Park: can we set autoscale to prioritize latency SLO over cost?
[00:06:52] Leah Armstrong: yes, you can set autoscale policies to keep headroom for p95 targets; our console exposes SLO-first policies and cost-aware policies.
[00:07:02] [00:07:02] Samir Patel: quick callouts: we'll need the sample traffic by Tue, and leah will do the test runs mid-next week.
[00:07:09] Dr. Maya Singh: timeline wise procurement wants to decide by end of April, pilot start first week of May ideally.
[00:07:15] Samir Patel: that's doable — we'll prioritize the numbers for you.
[00:07:20] [00:07:20] (later, detailed Q&A)
[00:22:35] Carlos Rios: deep dive on batching — how does continuous batching affect tail latency for small requests?
[00:22:40] Leah Armstrong: continuous batching groups concurrently inflight requests but has safeguards to not exceed latency SLOs; there's a latency floor introduced by batching wait-time, but with adaptive thresholds we see p95 reductions overall because GPU utilization is better.
[00:22:56] Jorge Alvarado: any chance of negative interactions with our request priority? we have system requests and user-initiated ones.
[00:23:03] Drew Matthews: priority routing is supported — you can tag requests and give them priority queues; lower-priority work will be preempted or scheduled differently.
[00:23:12] [00:23:12] Speaker 4: (faint)
[00:23:20] Ellen Park: we also use an internal rate limiter. how would Redwood integrate?
[00:23:24] Leah Armstrong: there are per-token and per-route rate limits; we can align with your sidecar rate limiter or you can delegate to Redwood for global quotas.
[00:23:34] Carlos Rios: last technical nit — if a streaming connection drops client-side, does the server keep the generation to allow resumption?
[00:23:40] Drew Matthews: yes, we keep partial KV cache and support reconnection strategies for short durations; longer reconnects may require re-generation.
[00:23:49] [00:23:49] (affirms)
[00:34:10] Samir Patel: okay wrapping up — recap of next steps: share tco template, leah runs baseline, customer shares traffic/profile, schedule pilot kickoff.
[00:34:22] Dr. Maya Singh: sounds good. thanks all, we'll gather the sample prompts and traffic by Tue.
[00:34:29] Ellen Park: i'll assign SSO/security reviewer to loop in.
[00:34:33] Samir Patel: great, i'll send calendar invites and the runbook.
[00:34:38] [00:34:38] End of recording
